boundary_note: Bounded first pass for the frozen Sutherland's Station record (April 2, 1865) in the Appomattox Campaign [March-April 1865]. The Petersburg assault (VA089) is the same day. Humphreys commanded the Second Corps, and his account of its actions here is a participant's. Army-wide returns, campaign-wide loss and prisoner totals, the April 9 paroles and the retreat as a whole are context; they are not assigned to one record or added across records. Draft claims do not alter model inputs.

claims.value: The frozen force field reads 'Divisions' and the live field zero. Humphreys says the force was McGowan's, McRae's, Scales's and Cooke's brigades of Hill's corps under Heth, later under Cooke; Miles names the brigades he committed (Nugent's, Madill's under MacDougall, and Ramsey's).
claims.rationale: Formation lists only; no headcount for either side. None is adopted as a matched opening strength; live zeros are not measured absence.

The April 1 date in the captures list conflicts with the April 2 action and is preserved.

open_questions: Humphreys' own report (No. 21), the brigade reports of Nugent, MacDougall and Ramsey (Nos. 32, 38, 45), Cooke's, McGowan's and Heth's accounts, Sheridan's account of relinquishing the division (selected; cited under VA088) and the returns remain deferred.

NPS/CWSAC (the live NPS page and the frozen Arnold rows) is one family. Humphreys' The Virginia Campaign of ’64 and ’65 (1883) is an interested history by the commander of the Second Corps in this campaign, in the same author family as the registered From Gettysburg to the Rapidan; where it narrates his own corps it is a participant's account. It relies on the reports of Sheridan, Warren, Wright, Gibbon, Ewell and Fitzhugh Lee, on Confederate testimony before the Warren Court of Inquiry and on the returns, so it is not independent of those families. Lee's, Sheridan's, Bushrod Johnson's, Miles's, Gibbon's, Ewell's and Fitzhugh Lee's papers, printed in Official Records Series I, Volume XLVI, Part 1, are separate families of interested commanders' accounts; the volume is a shared container, not an additional witness. Report dates are not event times or proof of contemporary knowledge.
No automatic commander attribution, causal campaign score, morale/readiness number or battle/campaign double counting.
